_readme: Everything identical for every Comeet customer. A company record under profiles/companies/ names "platform": "comeet" and adds only what differs: slug, name, careers_url, api.endpoint (which carries both the uid and the per-company token) and health. Merged company-over-platform by profiles.resolve_profile, then validated as one document.

israel_filter._note: VERIFIED live 2026-08-13. post_fetch is the correct and only method here, per SKILL Step 5: the API has no location parameter at all - every query parameter tried (page, limit, offset, skip, and location-shaped ones) was ignored and returned the identical full board. So there is nothing to filter with before fetching; the single call returns every posting worldwide and relevance is decided on location.name. `structure: none` records that Comeet's API exposes no location filter, not that its hosted careers page lacks one.

api._note: The stable id is `uid` (e.g. '71.E67'), NOT `id` - Comeet has no top-level `id` field, and falling back to the link would produce a different key for the same posting the moment the slug in that URL changed. Verified 238 unique uids across the largest board in the set. `url_comeet_hosted_page` is an absolute www.comeet.com link; `url_active_page` also exists and points at the company's own branded careers page, but it is not always present and sometimes carries a tracking query - the hosted page is the one that is always there.

detail_fetch._note: VERIFIED live 2026-08-13 against the posting above, and measured across a random sample of Comeet companies. *** THIS REPLACES A BLOCK THAT WAS WRONG. *** It previously said method 'none' and justified that with 'the listing response carries `details` - an array of {name, value} sections holding the description'. That was written without being verified and is false: NEITHER the positions listing NOR the per-position API endpoint returns any description field. The consequence was not cosmetic - it left the experience filter unable to evaluate 105 of this project's 145 companies, so 72% of alerts arrived tagged 'undetermined' and untriaged. What is true: the hosted posting page carries the description inside a `POSITION_DATA = {...}` script assignment, at custom_fields.details, as a list of {name, value} sections whose names include 'Requirements'. method='html' cannot reach it - the page is an Angular app, so the text is not in the server-rendered DOM and no content_selector matches. Hence embedded_json. The section NAME becomes an <h3> via render_sections, and that heading promotion is what makes the unmarked bullets under 'Requirements' count as mandatory in experience.classify_block. COST: one plain GET per NEW posting, bounded by the run-wide MAX_DETAIL_FETCHES_PER_RUN of 40 - not per company. On a 3-hourly cron that is a handful of requests; a company reworking its whole board spends the cap and the overflow stays undetermined, which fails open like every other miss.

health._note: Both fields are overridden per company by the importer from that company's live verified count, because they are per-company facts and a platform-level default for them is meaningless. The defaults here are the SAFE direction: expected_min_jobs 0 disables the absolute floor (leaving the relative-collapse gate, which needs no per-profile number), and zero_is_plausible false means a company dropping to zero is treated as a fault rather than shrugged off.

notes: Endpoint template: https://www.comeet.co/careers-api/2.0/company/{uid}/positions?token={token}. One call, a flat JSON array, the entire board - no pagination of any kind (verified against vastdata/43.001, the largest board in the set at 238 postings: page, limit, offset and skip were all ignored and returned the same 238). THE TOKEN IS NOT THE UID - it is a separate per-company public value published in the JSON blob embedded in the company's Comeet-hosted board page (https://www.comeet.co/jobs/{slug}/{uid}), next to its company_uid. Using the uid as the token returns HTTP 400 'Account uid or token are not valid' for every company. The token is resolved ONCE at import time and baked into api.endpoint, never re-resolved at runtime: the board page is ~750 KB against a few KB for the API call, so resolving 104 tokens per run would add ~78 MB to every scheduled execution for data that effectively never changes. If a company's token is ever rotated its fetch returns HTTP 400, which surfaces as an ordinary fetch failure and reaches the maintenance alert after two consecutive runs. Full evidence: _onboarding/verify_report.md.
